_comment: Real-hardware training run. Matches the Physical Atari paper's Table 2,
except steps=648000 (= 6.0 h at 30 fps, the section 5.2 experiment).
ring_size is set explicitly for a 24 GB GPU. The agent's built-in default
is 400,000, which allocates 400000*3*128*128 = 18.31 GiB ON THE TRAINING
DEVICE and will OOM an RTX 4090 once model, activations, optimizer state,
and the CUDA context are added. 200,000 costs 9.16 GiB and holds 1.85 h of
experience instead of 3.70 h. That is a real algorithmic difference from the
paper (less replay diversity), so note it when comparing results.
On a card with more memory, raise it back toward 400000.
_comment_checkpoint: Save every 10000 steps (~11 min at the ~15 steps/s this rig actually
achieves). Without this the ONLY save happens after training AND the 50k
eval both finish -- roughly 12.5 h in -- so any crash loses the entire run.
A run driving real servos, a real camera and a USB serial bridge has many
more ways to die than a simulated one; the ESP32 already re-enumerated
_comment_game: Pong's control axis is LEFT/RIGHT, not up/down -- the paddle looks like it
moves vertically but the ROM reads the joystick's left/right axis. Measured:
minimal_action_set = [NOOP, FIRE, RIGHT, LEFT, RIGHTFIRE, LEFTFIRE];
random UP/DOWN scores -41 (paddle never moves), random LEFT/RIGHT -30.
So SERVO 51 is the critical actuator here and servo 52 is unused.
_comment_action_set: Pong's paddle, WITHOUT the fire button.
ALE's minimal set for pong is [0,1,3,4,11,12] = NOOP, FIRE, RIGHT, LEFT,
RIGHTFIRE, LEFTFIRE. Fire does nothing for the paddle, and on this robot
the fire linkage is mechanically disconnected, so FIRE aliases onto NOOP,
RIGHTFIRE onto RIGHT and LEFTFIRE onto LEFT. The agent then sees six
actions with only three distinct consequences and has to learn its way out
of a distinction that does not exist -- while the fire servo moves on half
of all steps for nothing. [0,3,4] is NOOP/RIGHT/LEFT.
NOTE THE DOUBLE BRACKETS. Experiment takes the cartesian product of every
list-valued key, so "action_set": [0,3,4] would silently run THREE
experiments with action_set = 0, then 3, then 4. Wrapping it in an outer
list makes it one value. Check the printed 'Total experiment
Pong still plays without FIRE -- it auto-serves. Verified in ale_py:
random LEFT/RIGHT only scores from step 255.
